response: A spinal subdural hematoma (SSDH) can be a sequela of a ruptured intracranial aneurysm. Although the exact mechanism is unclear, it is speculated that the SSDH may have migrated from the intracranial subdural space, possibly due to low cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure caused by continuous drainage and intrathecal thrombolytic therapy. It is essential to recognize SSDH as a potential complication of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) accompanied by an intracranial subdural hematoma.
